A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, ten tables, ten figures, and Appendices A–E are readable and support a reliable comparison, including material relocated between sections.

before.justification: v1 reports original vote-rigging simulations using Chatbot Arena historical votes, classifier evaluations, ablations, and defense experiments in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including simulated ranking changes, model-identification accuracy, and defense evaluations.

M1.justification: The target-only strategies, Omni-BT and Omni-On objectives and voting procedures, classifier training objective, and vote-filtering algorithm are unchanged in Sections 3 and 7 and Appendices B and E.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same historical votes covering 129 models, the 25-model HC3/Quora case study, five additional unrecognized models, length-control leaderboard scenario, and 22 additional targets in Appendix C.2.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same T-Tie, T-Abstain, T-Random, T-Normal, and no-rigging comparisons, as applicable, including the idealized T-Abstain comparison in Table 4. Newly cited social-voting studies are not added experimental baselines.

E3.justification: The 90%/10% historical/other-user vote division, initial 20,000-vote simulations, classifier training settings, evaluation sample sizes, and stress-test conditions are retained. Appendix A.2's change from 'battles' to 'votes' aligns the wording with the existing Figure 5 caption rather than changing the evaluation.

E4.justification: The same analyses examine identification errors, sampling probabilities, concurrent voting, unseen prompts and models, training-corpus size, and defenses. Appendix A retains the same objective comparisons and score-update ablation; the response examples in Appendix D are also unchanged.

E5.justification: There is no change in uncertainty-reporting practices or the likelihood-based detection analysis. Neither version supplies repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or error bars for the rigging results.

E6.justification: The numerical entries, plotted results, and qualitative findings are unchanged across Tables 1–10 and Figures 1–10. For example, Table 10 retains average ranking improvements of +2.0 for Omni-BT, +2.1 for Omni-On, and +0.9 for T-Abstain.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(8) and the informal omni-property proof in Appendix A.1 are unchanged. Appendix A.2 now explicitly describes the model immediately above the target, repeating the definition already present in Section 3.2.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central claims: Chatbot Arena is vulnerable to vote rigging, omnipresent strategies improve efficiency and can operate without the target appearing in a battle, and effective defenses remain challenging.

C2.justification: Both versions retain the proof-of-concept qualification, explanations for keeping initial BT scores fixed, interpretations of robustness and length-control vulnerabilities, and limitations of the tested defenses. The added social-voting discussion concerns research positioning rather than new result interpretations.

D1.justification: Classifier implementation, training duration and hardware, response-length filtering, markdown removal, model lists, and code/data access links are unchanged. Moving the model-identification literature discussion out of Appendix B.1 does not remove implementation information.

R1.justification: Section 8 adds a focused discussion of social-voting manipulation with eight additional cited works, distinguishing Chatbot Arena through anonymous candidates and rigging efficiency. It also adds Liu et al. (2024), RMbench, to the evaluation-bias discussion. The model-identification literature paragraph is relocated from Appendix B.1.

P1.justification: v2 expands Related Work and consolidates the model-identification discussion there. Elsewhere, changes are localized wording and typo corrections, an appendix-heading refinement, and clarification in Appendix A.2; the overall narrative and section organization remain largely intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds conference-style title rules, running headers, page numbers, and a proceedings notice, with corresponding text and float reflow and a small caption edit. The same figures and tables remain, with unchanged graphical content and table structures.

improvement.justification: The added social-voting discussion in Section 8 provides useful scholarly context and explains how anonymous candidates distinguish this setting. Consolidating model-identification literature and making small clarity corrections also improve readability. These are limited gains because the methods, empirical evidence, theoretical support, and limitations remain unchanged.
